messages.text:
Ive got a bitaxe 601 that isnt even 9 months old and it stopped
functioning,  i need to get it in and repaired or replaced.

Hi there,

Thanks for the details, and sorry the 601 has gone quiet on you. I handle the hardware side here, so let me get this triaged properly with you. On these boards "stopped working" splits into two very different causes, and the quick checks below tell us which one it is. If it turns out to be a board fault I will pass my findings straight to our hardware lead so the team can arrange the return, and you do not need to do anything else on that front.

First, the power side. On the Bitaxe Gamma 601 a failing or underpowered 5V brick is by far the most common cause of a unit that suddenly will not start, more common than the miner itself failing. The board wants a solid 5V supply able to hold around 5A to 6A without sagging. If you have another good quality 5V brick with the same barrel size, or a bench supply, please try it, and also try a different outlet and a different cable. If it comes back to life on the second supply, the miner is fine and the brick is the problem, and we can send you a proper one.

Second, what it actually does when you plug it in. Please tell me whether the small screen lights up at all, whether the fan spins for a moment or not at all, and whether any LED comes on. If the screen does light up, tell me exactly what it shows, word for word, including anything about chips, VREG or temperature. Messages along the lines of "0 chips", "cannot detect chips" or "VREG overheated" point at the voltage regulator on the board, which is a genuine board level fault and not something you can fix at home.

Third, if it does power up and simply is not hashing, that is usually not broken hardware at all. Check that you can reach AxeOS in a browser on the miner's IP, confirm the AxeOS version it is running, and check the pool settings: the stratum URL, the port and the worker name. A pool that changed its URL or a worker name that no longer matches your account will show a live unit doing nothing. In that case tell me the pool you are on and what the AxeOS overview page reports for hashrate and shares, and I will get it mining again.

To save a round trip, please reply with the order number it came on, a short video of the unit from the moment you plug it in until whatever happens stops, a clear photo of the screen if it lights up, and a photo of the serial number sticker. With those, plus the result of the second power supply, I can give the team a firm verdict without any guesswork.

One safety note: if you ever get a pop, sparks, smoke or a burning smell, unplug it at the wall straight away and do not power it again. Tell me if that happened and we stop testing right there.

Our team is offline for the evening and back tomorrow at 10am ET, so send those details whenever suits you and I will pick it up from there in this same thread.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

The unit will sometimes power up the fan, but that is all, no
screenl,led,light, or other signs of life. I put multimeter leads at
soldered joint for 5v power in and with the fan running it had 5.4v, the
same as if testing at power supply barrel with it not connected.
Note to the team: Verdict recorded as defective and handed back to Sarah; no reply sent from me on this turn.
